web_evidence.title: Mailer's Narrative Poetics: From Fiction to Nonfiction
web_evidence.note: Scholarly narratological study identifies The Naked and the Dead as Mailer's sole novel using a heterodiegetic-extradiegetic narrator comparable to traditional omniscient narration.

web_evidence.title: Understanding Conflict and Character: An Analysis of Norman Mailer's Narrative “The Naked and the Dead”
web_evidence.note: Scholarly article explicitly states that the novel employs third-person omniscient narration and explains that this perspective spans battlefield action, characters' inner crises, and Time Machine flashbacks.

web_evidence.title: Norman Mailer's Ripe Garbage
web_evidence.note: Credible critical review describes the narrator moving among the soldiers like an omniscient camera and periodically shifting to other characters and settings.

web_evidence.title: A Gentleman of Letters
web_evidence.note: Mailer's biographer explicitly distinguishes The Naked and the Dead as the major exception to Mailer's usual first-person practice and discusses its all-knowing third-person narrator.

search_log: Searched “The Naked and the Dead Norman Mailer point of view third person omniscient narrator” and found explicit whole-book classifications in a Tampere University narratology study and a scholarly journal article.

Searched for authorized excerpts and first-chapter material; opened Macmillan and Library of America edition pages, but they provided structural summaries rather than sustained prose or explicit grammatical-person evidence.

Searched “The Naked and the Dead narrative technique omniscient scholarly” and targeted university, journal, and Google Books results; the Tampere study identified the narrator as heterodiegetic-extradiegetic, while the journal article covered both the campaign and Time Machine sections.

Searched “The Naked and the Dead third-person Mailer novel” and opened critical corroboration from The Baffler and Mailer biographical scholarship; no credible source described sustained first- or second-person base sections.

Ran exact-phrase searches for suspicious quotes: the Tolstoy passage belongs to The Spooky Art, the writing-quality passage comes from the anniversary introduction, and the Israel passage is embedded speech by Goldstein's grandfather.
person_note: The diagnostic novel passages repeatedly use a nonparticipating narrator who moves among Roth, Red, Croft, Gallagher, Margaret, and groups of soldiers while reporting private memories, emotions, and thoughts. The present-tense Time Machine material remains third person rather than forming a different-person strand. First- and second-person forms in the sample occur in dialogue, generic maxims, paratext, or material from another Mailer work; the anniversary-introduction quotation is also not story narration. Two independent scholarly sources explicitly classify the whole novel as third-person omniscient or heterodiegetic-extradiegetic, with credible critical sources corroborating that structure. No credible contrary or alternating-person evidence was found; uncertainty is limited to a few clipped or context-poor individual quotes.
